description: Two-panel composite figure; both panels are data plots of Fe-Al (ferritic low-density) steels against Al content, x-axis "Al (wt%)" 0-25. (a) is a dual-ordinate tensile-property plot: left ordinate "Strength (MPa)" 0-800, right ordinate "Elongation (%)" 5-40. Four labelled series: TE (open triangles, read on the elongation axis) falls from near the 35% gridline at ~2 wt% Al to near the 10% gridline at 10 wt% Al; UE (filled triangles) lies between roughly the 200 and 350 MPa levels and decreases with Al; UTS (open circles) rises from about the 100 MPa gridline to the 470-480 MPa region at 10 wt% Al; YS (filled diamonds) rises to a maximum between the 500 and 600 MPa gridlines at ~13 wt% Al, then drops below 200 MPa and stays almost flat to 25 wt% Al. Vertical dashed lines divide the composition axis into fields labelled A2, K1, A2+DO3, DO3 and B2. (b) plots work hardening rate (GPa, 0-20) versus Al (wt%) with the same phase-field divisions: about 1 GPa below 7 wt% Al, a steep rise to a sharp peak between the 15 and 20 GPa gridlines at ~15-16 wt% Al (DO3 field), then a fall to ~6-7 GPa at 20-24 wt% Al. Together the panels show Al solid-solution/ordering hardening of Fe-Al raising strength but sharply reducing elongation.

observations.observation: Panel (a) uses two ordinates: left 'Strength (MPa)' spanning 0-800 and right 'Elongation (%)' spanning 5-40, with x-axis 'Al (wt%)' from 0 to 25.

In (a), the YS series (filled diamonds) rises with Al content to a maximum between the 500 and 600 MPa gridlines at about 13 wt% Al, then falls sharply below the 200 MPa gridline and remains nearly flat out to 25 wt% Al.
In (a), UTS (open circles) increases monotonically from about the 100 MPa gridline near 1 wt% Al to approximately the 470-480 MPa level at 10 wt% Al.

In (a), TE (open triangles, read against the right elongation axis) decreases from near the 35% gridline at low Al content to near the 10% gridline at 10 wt% Al, and UE (filled triangles) lies between roughly 200 and 350 MPa and also decreases with Al.
Both panels carry vertical dashed lines that divide the Al axis into composition ranges labelled at the top as A2, K1, A2+DO3, DO3 and B2, the last transition occurring above about 23 wt% Al.

In (b), the work hardening rate (GPa) is about 1 GPa for Al < 7 wt%, rises steeply to a sharp peak between the 15 and 20 GPa gridlines at about 15-16 wt% Al, then falls to roughly 6-7 GPa at 20-24 wt% Al.
The work hardening-rate peak in (b) lies inside the DO3 phase field, while the low-value plateau lies in the A2 field.
The caption states that (a) shows tensile properties vs. Al content including the influence of different lattice structure and the solid-solution hardening effect of Al in Fe, citing refs [24,37].
The caption states that (b) is the work hardening rate measured over the 1-1.5% plastic strain range as a function of Al content, citing ref [38].

The citing text states that Al creates marked solid-solution strengthening in ferrite with about a 40 MPa/wt% increase in yield strength, following Suzuki's theory of solid-solution hardening of BCC alloys [24,37,38].
The citing text states the yield strength of the Fe-Al solid solution increases with Al up to 13% (22 at.%), then falls rapidly between 13 and 15% and remains almost constant up to 25% Al.

The citing text states that at room temperature total tensile elongation decreases with increasing Al and that a transition from ductile to brittle fracture without necking occurs in the 8-10% Al range.

The citing text states the work hardening rate is low for disordered Fe-Al alloys with less than 7% Al, rises to a sharp peak at 16% Al with formation of the ordered state, and falls to a moderate value above 20% Al, attributing hardening mainly to shearing of ordered phases by super dislocations.

subfigures.description: Dual-ordinate tensile-property plot of Fe-Al steels: left axis Strength (MPa) 0-800, right axis Elongation (%) 5-40, x-axis Al (wt%) 0-25. Labelled series YS (filled diamonds, peaks between the 500 and 600 MPa gridlines at ~13 wt% Al then collapses), UTS (open circles, rising), UE (filled triangles, decreasing, ~200-350 MPa) and TE (open triangles, elongation axis, falling from ~35% to ~10%). Vertical dashed lines mark phase fields A2, K1, A2+DO3, DO3, B2.

Work hardening rate (GPa, 0-20) versus Al (wt%), square markers with a connecting line: ~1 GPa below 7 wt% Al, steep rise to a sharp maximum between the 15 and 20 GPa gridlines at ~15-16 wt% Al, then decline to ~6-7 GPa above 20 wt% Al. Same dashed phase-field lines and top labels A2, K1, A2+DO3, DO3, B2.
